deep.reconstruction:
Notation: in E477 Euler writes ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) for the series Σ_{k≥1} (1/k^m)(1 + 1/2^n + … + 1/k^n). In modern terms this is S(m,n) = Σ_k H_k^{(n)}/k^m, a double zeta value in which the inner sum includes k. He writes ∫1/z^p for ζ(p).

End of §20. The 'second method' (term-by-term rearrangement of products of series, essentially the stuffle/harmonic-product relations together with some partial-fraction identities) yields, in even weight m+n, the known relations among ζ(2), ζ(4), ζ(6), …. For example it gives ζ(10) = (10/11) ζ(4)ζ(6), the case k = 5 of Σ_{j=1}^{k-1} ζ(2j)ζ(2k−2j) = (k+½) ζ(2k). Euler stresses that these come out without any appeal to the quadrature of the circle, i.e. without knowing that ζ(2k) is a rational multiple of π^{2k}.

He then remarks that one would have expected analogous relations among the odd-power sums ζ(3), ζ(5), … in odd weight. Instead, the relations obtained there partly coincide with one another, so nothing at all can be concluded. He calls this 'defect of full determination' worthy of every attention.

§21. In every order one series is always fully determined, namely S(m+n−1, 1) = Σ H_k/k^{w−1}, where w = m+n is the weight. Euler lists the even-weight case:
- S(3,1) = (3/2) ζ(2)² − (5/2) ζ(4)
- S(5,1) = 3 ζ(2)ζ(4) − ½ ζ(3)² − (7/2) ζ(6)
- S(7,1) = 3 ζ(2)ζ(6) − ζ(3)ζ(5) + (3/2) ζ(4)² − (9/2) ζ(8)
- S(9,1) = 3 ζ(2)ζ(8) − ζ(3)ζ(7) + 3 ζ(4)ζ(6) − ½ ζ(5)² − (11/2) ζ(10)
- S(11,1) = 3 ζ(2)ζ(10) − ζ(3)ζ(9) + 3 ζ(4)ζ(8) − ζ(5)ζ(7) + (3/2) ζ(6)² − (13/2) ζ(12)

The pattern for odd m is:
- even-even products ζ(2i)ζ(2j) get coefficient 3 (3/2 for a square);
- odd-odd products get coefficient −1 (−½ for a square);
- the single term is −((m+2)/2) ζ(m+1).

The page continues into the odd-weight table and the unified 'interpolated' formula 2 S(m,1) = (m+2) ζ(m+1) − Σ_{j=1}^{m−2} ζ(m−j) ζ(j+1), which is Euler's classical formula for Σ H_k/k^m. The even-weight list here is that classical formula plus 2·[Σ_{j=1}^{k−1} ζ(2j)ζ(2k−2j) − (k+½) ζ(2k)], which is zero.

The problem served: evaluating linear Euler sums / double zeta values in closed form in terms of single zeta values, and understanding why the system of relations is incomplete.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All five even-weight formulas were checked numerically against the known values via ζ(2k) = rational·π^{2k}: S(3,1) = (5/4)ζ(4), S(5,1) = (7/4)ζ(6) − ½ζ(3)², and the m = 7, 9, 11 cases each reduce to the classical Euler formula using Σ ζ(2j)ζ(2k−2j) = (k+½)ζ(2k).

Historical-mathematical caveat: Euler's claim that his method leaves 'one determination' missing in all orders except 1, 2, 3, 5 includes odd weights (e.g. weight 5, 7). There, by Euler's own later-recognized theorem (made rigorous by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn 1995), all double zeta values reduce to products of single zetas. The gap is therefore a deficiency of the relations he used (lacking the shuffle/integral relations), not an intrinsic one.

ideas.what: Closed form of Σ H_k/k^m for odd m (even weight) in terms of products of zeta values, written in a form with coefficients 3 / −1 on even/odd products
ideas.modern_name: Euler's formula for linear Euler sums / double zeta reduction ζ(m,1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1775/76); later proofs by Nielsen, Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn, and others
ideas.where_published: E477 itself (Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 20, 1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Observation that the series-manipulation (stuffle-type) relations reproduce the relations among ζ(2), ζ(4), ζ(6), … without using that ζ(2k) is a rational multiple of π^{2k}
ideas.modern_name: Double shuffle relations imply Euler's convolution identity Σ ζ(2j)ζ(2k−2j) = (k+½)ζ(2k)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed in modern form by Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier (2006) and in the MZV literature

ideas.what: Expectation, and failure, of analogous relations among products of odd zeta values; the 'defect of full determination' flagged as worthy of attention
ideas.modern_name: Absence of algebraic relations among odd zeta values (conjectural algebraic independence); insufficiency of stuffle-only relations for double zetas
ideas.usually_credited_to: Modern conjectures (Zagier, Goncharov, Brown on motivic MZVs)

missed.claim: Euler explicitly notes that the combinatorial relations among his double series yield the even-zeta product relations independently of π. He also explicitly expected, and failed to find, analogous relations among odd zeta values, calling the failure worthy of all attention. This is an early statement of the modern dichotomy: double shuffle produces the even-weight period relations, while odd zeta values admit no such relations. Whether historians explicitly credit Euler with this observation is unclear to me (unsure); it is likely known to MZV specialists who read E477.
missed.quote: ex quo etiam expectare licuisset, pro ordinibus, quibus m+n est numerus impar, similem relationem inter summas potestatum imparium prodire debuisse, quod autem longe secus vsu venit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical anchor for the double-shuffle derivation of ζ(2k) relations (Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier) and for the expected transcendence/independence of odd zeta values. It is mainly of historiographical interest, not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The formulas are Euler's well-known sums Σ H_k/k^m, merely written in an alternative but equivalent form. The meta-remarks (relations among even zetas obtained without π; the puzzling absence of odd analogues) are insightful and anticipate modern themes. However, E477 is heavily studied in the MZV community, so this is likely at least partially known.

In the m = 9 and m = 11 lines, the multiplication dot between ∫1/z^5 ∫1/z^5 (and ∫1/z^5 ∫1/z^7) is missing in print; it denotes a product.
